# Strang and Herman — Calculus Volume 1 (OpenStax, 2016)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Gilbert Strang and Edwin “Jed” Herman, *Calculus Volume 1* (Houston: OpenStax, 2016), §4.10, https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/4-10-antiderivatives.

**Shortened note:** Strang and Herman, *Calculus Volume 1*, §4.10.

**Bibliography:** Strang, Gilbert, and Edwin “Jed” Herman. *Calculus Volume 1*. Houston: OpenStax, 2016. https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/4-10-antiderivatives.

## Essay use

Strang and Herman states the standard interval-relative family of antiderivatives. It gives §3/#0 a precise technical boundary for the integration-constant image: differentiation does not determine a unique antiderivative without a constant, but this fact does not supply a metaphysics of provenance.

**Claim boundary:** the text establishes a theorem about antiderivatives on an interval. It does not prove QL’s eightfold, `∞/dx`, the return to zero, or any psychological/metaphysical conclusion.

<a id="strang-herman-2016-openstax-calculus-v1-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `strang-herman-2016-openstax-calculus-v1-q002` — interval-qualified uniqueness
^strang-herman-2016-openstax-calculus-v1-q002

> “if G is an antiderivative of f over I, there is a constant C for which G(x)=F(x)+C over I.”

- **Locator:** §4.10, Theorem 4.14, “General Form of an Antiderivative,” item 2.
